# 7450 - 2x2 AND-OR-INVERT (7450 - 7451 - 7460)

Package DIP-14 · family 74 · catalogue file [catalog/chips/7450.json](https://github.com/RetroCoreLabs/RetroSchematic/blob/master/src/catalog/chips/7450.json)

## Symbol

| As printed in ND-13.003.01, page 12 | Drawn in ND style | Drawn in modern style |
|---|---|---|
| ![7450 as printed in the 1976 symbol manual](../../../catalog/symbols/nd1976/7450.png) | ![7450 drawn in nd style](../../../catalog/symbols/nd1976/shapes/aoi-2x28.png) | ![7450 drawn in modern style](../../../catalog/symbols/modern/shapes/aoi-2x28.png) |

Boxes stacked on the left (the AND parts) feeding an X box (the OR-invert). The manual notes the four-input gates are 7460 circuits (expanders). 7451 is drawn the same way.

How to tell it on a drawing: Stacked boxes feeding an X box = AND-OR-INVERT.

All symbols: [symbol catalogue](../../SYMBOL-CATALOG.md).

| 14 | VCC | power |  | +5 V |

## Functions

| Output pin | Formula | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| 8 | 1Y = NOT ((1A AND 1B) OR (1C AND 1D) OR X) | Gate 1 (expandable): 1Y is low when 1A and 1B are both high, or 1C and 1D are both high, or an expander on X/X' has all its inputs high. X = output of a 7460 expander. |
| 6 | 2Y = NOT ((2A AND 2B) OR (2C AND 2D)) | Gate 2: 2Y is low when 2A and 2B are both high, or 2C and 2D are both high. |

## Propagation delays

| From | To | Edge | Typ ns | Max ns | Conditions |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| any | Y | PLH | 13 | 22 | VCC 5 V, TA 25 C, CL 15 pF, RL 400 ohm, expander pins open |
| any | Y | PHL | 8 | 15 | VCC 5 V, TA 25 C, CL 15 pF, RL 400 ohm, expander pins open |
| 7460 expander input | 1Y | PLH | 15 | 30 | VCC 5 V, TA 25 C, CL 15 pF, RL 400 ohm, from an input of a 7460 expander |
| 7460 expander input | 1Y | PHL | 10 | 20 | VCC 5 V, TA 25 C, CL 15 pF, RL 400 ohm, from an input of a 7460 expander |

## Notes

The manual title groups 7450, 7451 and 7460; this file describes the 7450 (one gate expandable, one not). The datasheet gives no minimum propagation delays; the path-delay function uses 0 ns for the minimum.
